title: Potato and Cheese Pierogi
subtitle: Polish boiled dumplings filled with mashed potato and cheddar
excerpt: Soft dough pockets filled with mashed potato and melted cheddar, boiled until tender then pan-fried in butter until golden. The caramelised onion inside makes all the difference. Worth the effort.
sourceNotes: Pierogi are Poland's national dumpling and appear across Central and Eastern European cuisines under different names. The potato and cheese filling is one of the most traditional styles.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked on a lined tray, then transfer to a bag. Boil from frozen for 5 to 6 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Make in bulk and freeze in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: Keep the dough covered while you work to stop it drying out. Roll it thin but not so thin it tears when you seal it.
Make the filling first. Cook the diced onion in a little butter over low heat for 20 minutes until golden and sweet.
Mix the mashed potato with the cheddar and caramelised onion. Season well. Set aside to cool.
Make the dough. Mix flour, eggs and soured cream in a bowl. Knead for 3 minutes until smooth. Wrap and rest for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough on a floured surface to 3mm thick. Cut out circles about 9cm across.
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre of each circle. Fold over and press the edges firmly to seal.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pierogi in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and the dough is cooked through.
Drain well. Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the boiled pierogi for 2 minutes per side until golden.

items.cause: Edges were not pressed firmly enough or dough too thin.
items.fix: Press firmly and use a fork to crimp the seal.

items.symptom: Dough is too stiff to roll.
items.cause: Not enough moisture or needs more resting time.
items.fix: Add a teaspoon of water and knead again.

items.cause: Too much filling in each piece.
items.fix: Use a heaped teaspoon only, not more.
